title: Custom Request Processing
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of custom request processing in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to request timing.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers custom request processing within middleware, cors, and request processing. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use custom request processing to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is clear input/output contracts, field validation, serialization and safe defaults.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Custom Request Processing matters because it is part of middleware, cors, and request processing. In practice, focus on clear input/output contracts, field validation, serialization and safe defaults. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Request timing
items.text: Use request timing as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Logging request metadata
items.text: For logging request metadata, collect measurable evidence from a local or staging environment. Keep configuration environment-specific, avoid logging secrets, establish a rollback path, and do not claim performance or availability without measurements.

items.title: Error handling across request processing
items.text: Use error handling across request processing to make behavior observable and repeatable. Specify one normal case, one invalid or missing-input case, and the expected status or diagnostic. A passing happy path alone is not enough evidence.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Custom Request Processing
content_blocks.run_instructions: Try one existing-style ID and the documented missing-resource case.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Request timing”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Custom Request Processing”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Request timing” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Custom Request Processing, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Custom Request Processing belongs to the broader goal of clear input/output contracts, field validation, serialization and safe defaults.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
